- When sentiment is high (≥0.3) and forecast is significantly above true outcome, reduce forecast by 5–10% to avoid overreaction.  
- If forecast spikes sharply after a low sentiment period, cap the peak at 10–15% above recent high to prevent overshoot.  
- When true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 65), adjust forecast downward by 2–5% to reflect momentum.  
- If sentiment is low (≤0.1) and forecast is consistently above true, reduce forecast by 3–7% to align with subdued market sentiment.  
- For 30-day horizon, if forecast is consistently 2–3% above true for 5+ days, apply a downward bias correction of 1–2% per day to reflect lagged adjustment.
